cells.tense: You are here at the pen, and the direction you feel is the one you are already moving in.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: On the next stretch you walk beside someone, find out how the road looks from where they stand, and let their first reply sit before you answer.
cells.core:
You can feel the pull of a good direction and your body is already loose toward it, not braced. You take the next practical thing because it belongs to what you're moving toward, and the patience holds because the patience has somewhere to point. The light is far enough off that you aren't gripping it, close enough that you aren't lost.

On the next stretch you walk beside someone, find out how the road looks from where they stand. Then wait past their first reply — the second one is usually the truer. You don't have to fix it, and you don't have to agree. The pull you're following gets truer when it isn't only yours.
cells.sheetLine: You move because the direction is real, not because it's close.
cells.verb: Holding the body steady along a line you can see but have not yet walked
cells.place: A place oriented toward light that has not arrived

cells.tense: You will have built the whole arrival before the light has shown you the next turn.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: This week, when emotion shows up across the table, weigh with your own hand what your response takes from the other person and what it gives, then act.
cells.core:
The light ahead is real and you're building the road to it in advance — pouring, planning, pushing an arrival forward past what any of it can carry yet. Strength that stays a whisper when it's paced picks up scaffolding when it isn't, and the ones beside you on the road feel that weight, whether they mention it or not. What holds without forcing is still yours to have.

When emotion shows up across the table, don't decide fast. Weigh, with your own hand, what your response takes from the other person and what it gives, and then act. That weighing is the steady way back toward the light, because it moves at the speed of what is actually there.

cells.tense: You were facing a direction that has since moved, and you are still standing at the turn.
cells.act: drop one condition you set and take the step
cells.ask: Name one requirement you have placed before the next step, set it down, and step forward without it.
cells.core:
The direction you felt is still yours, and the version of arriving you had planned is not the one on offer. Your strength is still in the body that carries you; the bracing where the light used to shine has stayed, and it has become the stance. You know the direction. You are not facing it.

Letting go of one thing is enough. Name the requirement you've put before the next step — usually it sounds like needing something first — and set it down. Then step forward without it. You are not surrendering the direction. You are giving the light a road to reach you on.

cells.tense: The pen has been down in a room where you are still writing every wall that holds it up.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin some small undertaking this week with no plan for how it ends, because the starting is the pleasure you keep coming back to.
cells.core:
You have been showing people the light — laying steady floors under their directions — and the version you'd tell has you simply passing through on your own. The pull that keeps you aimed is real and it is yours. What has gone quiet is you pointing at it where it could be seen, as if the aiming were borrowed and only the work were yours.

Before you were holding the line for other people, you were someone who noticed what was good and went toward it first. Begin some small undertaking this week with no plan for how it ends, because the starting is the pleasure you keep coming back to. The light on your own face comes back when you turn toward it on your own errand.

The reader might object that ambition and hope were never the trouble; only the body's lag was. The ask survives being wrong because it works whether the person is directed or merely tired.
